pr_title: planner, util/ranger: recognize the best matching index stats more accurately for OR list in `Selectivity()`
pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?


Issue Number: close #54323

Problem Summary:

See https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/54323#issuecomment-2197278283

In the current implementation of `Selectivity()`, if the expression is an OR list, it's unable to recognize the best matching stats to use.

In the case of the issue, it thinks the index (a,b,c) and index (b) are the same in terms of matching/covering the expression. So it chooses index (b) according to another rule that says fewer columns are better.

### What changed and how does it work?

The rationale is to introduce a simple strategy to distinguish between different index stats when matching against an OR list.

Here I want to introduce the minimum number of "access conditions" among all OR list items as the criterion. Please see comments in `pkg/planner/util/path.go` for examples. This should be a simple and reliable criterion.

Since the related code path is long, several different places need changes:
- Collect `MinAccessCondsForDNFCond`. (`pkg/util/ranger/detacher.go`)
- To store and pass this information, I need to add a field to `DetachRangeResult`, `AccessPath`, and `StatsNode` respectively.
- Use this information. (`pkg/planner/cardinality/selectivity.go`)
- I also did a small refactor to try to make `GetUsableSetsByGreedy()` cleaner.

issue_context.title: large overestimation when where conditions contain OR and matches several indexes with different selectivity
comments:
This corresponds to two places that need to be improved:
1. The root cause
In this case, `Selectivity()` can't correctly match the stats to the filters. It should prefer stats on (iabc) for estimation, but finally chooses stats on (ib).
2. The root cause results in the overestimation of `DataSource.stats.RowCount`, and then the logic here brings the overestimation into the index range scan of index (iabc), then causes choosing the bad plan.
https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/854a4e3303003e3f8c1151da27e539337dcf8277/pkg/planner/core/logical_plans.go#L1599-L1601

The steps:

1. [`GetUsableSetsByGreedy` uses incorrect statistics to estimate the selectivity of the indexes.](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/854a4e3303003e3f8c1151da27e539337dcf8277/pkg/planner/core/logical_plans.go#L1599-L1601)
2. [`deriveIndexPathStats` employs an unperfect algorithm to update the `CountAfterAccess`.](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/854a4e3303003e3f8c1151da27e539337dcf8277/pkg/planner/core/logical_plans.go#L1599-L1601)
3. [`skylinePruning` prunes the ib index due to the `compareCandidates`.](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/2abd334934cd307012ae07b80849999155efd2e1/pkg/planner/core/find_best_task.go#L705)
4. [`compareTaskCost` chooses the table full scan due to the overestimated `CountAfterAccess`.](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/2abd334934cd307012ae07b80849999155efd2e1/pkg/planner/core/find_best_task.go#L348)
